newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FTC, Abbott settle over ad claims.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FTC, Abbott settle over ad claims.

text.p: Abbott Laboratories Inc. has agreed to settle Federal Trade Commission charges that it made false and unsubstantiated claims about its Ensure nutritional beverages, the agency said late Thursday.

It alleged that Abbott, in an extensive advertising campaign, represented that many doctors recommend Ensure as a meal supplement and replacement for healthy adults, including those in their thirties and forties.

Abbott agreed not to make any claim about doctors or other professionals recommending food, dietary or nutritional supplements or about any other such backing without competent and reliable evidence to support it, the FTC said.

Jodie Bernstein, director of the agency's bureau of consumer protection, said that nutritional beverages like Ensure may provide a benefit to people with medical conditions that make it difficult to eat or to replace a skipped meal.
"Abbott went too far, however," Bernstein said, "when it suggested that doctors recommend Ensure for healthy, active people, like those pictured in the ads, in order to stay active and healty."
